Order 
1
.  Learned counsel for the appellant is heard on the question of admission.

2. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company being aggrieved by award dated 24.7.2024, passed in MACC No.4/2021, by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Depalpur, District Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.22,30,296/- has been awarded to the respondents/claimants No.1 to 3 by way of compensation.
3. As per the claimants, on 7.12.2019, Kalyan Singh, husband of claimant No. 1 and father of claimants No. 2 and 3, was going on his motorcycle from Depalpur to Betma.

When he reached Village Harnasa, respondent No. 4 drove the offending vehicle Bolero loading pickup bearing registration No.MP-09-GG- 5886 which was owned by respondent No. 5 and was insured with the appellant in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motorcycle as a result of which he fell down and received grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment but eventually expired.

Thereafter the claimants filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.25,00,000/- to them by way of compensation.
The application was contested by the appellant and respondents No. 4 and 5 by filing their written statement to the same.

The Insurance Company took a defence inter alia that it is a case of false involvement and the offending vehicle has been implicated into the accident with malafide intention only for seeking compensation.
The accident in question has not been caused by the offending vehicle hence, the Insurance Company is not liable for payment of any amount of compensation.

5. Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties, by the impugned award, the claims Tribunal has held that the claimants have satisfactorily proved that the accident in question was caused by the offending vehicle itself and that the same was due to the rash and negligent driving of respondent No.4.
The offending vehicle was insured with the appellant at the time of accident which is hence liable for payment of the compensation amount.

In consequence,
compensation as aforesaid has been awarded in favour of the claimants.
6. This appeal has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that it is a case of false implication of the vehicle.
At the time of accident, a Marg was registered but the registration number of the offending vehicle was not disclosed.
During the entire Marg proceedings, the same was not brought on record.
The FIR in the matter is delayed by eight days, which by itself is sufficient for raising a presumption that it is a case of false implication.
The surveyor of the appellant had also conducted due inquiry in which he had found that no accident with the offending vehicle as alleged ever took place.
He was also examined before the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9768 3 MA-9843-2024 Tribunal.
There was no reason to discredit his statement and it should have been held that the offending vehicle was not involved in the accident in question.
The income of the deceased assessed exorbitant.
It is hence submitted that the impugned award deserves to be set aside.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the appellant and have perused the record.
8. As per the claimants, at the time when the accident took place, the deceased Kalyan Singh was going on a motorcycle From Jalodiya to his village Harnasa.
On another motorcycle Jitendra was coming at the back.
When both the motorcycle reached the spot of the accident, the offending vehicle dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased.

Jitendra is an eye-witness to the incident and he has been examined before the Tribunal as A.W.-2 and he has specifically stated that the accident in question was caused by the offending vehicle itself.
He has given the registration number of the vehicle also.
In his cross-examination, nothing could be brought out to disbelieve his statement or to show that the same is false in any manner.
His statement is reasonable and cogent and has rightly been acted upon by the claims Tribunal.
9. While in the Marg which was registered initially, the vehicle number may not has been mentioned but the same was specifically mentioned in the FIR which was registered.
Registration number of the vehicle is available at all the places in the record of the criminal case.

The period between the Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. ... vs Smt. Jamnabai on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144656959/
2 date of accident and registration of FIR is only about 7 to 8 days, hence, it cannot be said that the FIR has been delayed in any manner.

sentences.text:
The statement of the surveyor of the appellant namely Vaibhav Sharma would be a statement of the appellant in its own favour NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9768 4 MA-9843-2024 and is not a statement of any independent witness.
The report prepared by the said surveyor hence also cannot be relied upon to the extent to discredit the version of the eye-witness.
10. The claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.26,000/- per month which has been submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant to be highly excessive.

However, from the record, it is observed that the deceased was working as secretary in Janpad Panchayat,
Depalpur, District Indore.
The salary slips of the deceased of around August, 2019 were produced before the Tribunal as Ex. P/11 to P/15 in which his income was stated as 26000/- per month.

A perusal of the said pay slips indicated that it was the actual income of the deceased and there was no reason to disbelieve the same, hence, they have rightly been acted upon by the claims Tribunal and compensation as aforesaid has been awarded to the claimants.
11. Thus in view of the aforesaid discussion, I do not find any error having been committed by the Claims Tribunal in passing the impugned award.
The appeal is hence found to be devoid of any merits and is hereby dismissed.

(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE VD Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd. ... vs Smt. Jamnabai on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144656959/
